content_voiceover: This is the IMWG response criteria table for multiple myeloma, spanning MRD assessment down to minimal response. Flow MRD negative means no aberrant clonal plasma cells by next generation flow, sensitive to one in one hundred thousand cells, and sequencing MRD negative uses next generation sequencing at the same sensitivity. Imaging plus MRD negative adds disappearance of abnormal PET tracer uptake, and sustained MRD negative requires that negativity be confirmed a minimum of one year apart. For standard categories, stringent complete response is a complete response plus a normal free light chain ratio and no clonal cells on marrow biopsy. Complete response requires negative immunofixation in serum and urine, disappearance of plasmacytomas, and less than five percent bone marrow plasma cells. Very good partial response allows a detectable but non-quantifiable M protein by immunofixation, or a ninety percent or greater reduction in serum M protein. Partial response is a fifty percent or greater reduction in serum M protein with a matching urine reduction, and minimal response is a twenty five to forty nine percent reduction.
keypoints: MRD negativity requires NGF or NGS sensitivity of at least 1 in 100,000 cells
Sustained MRD-negative: confirmed by marrow and imaging, at least 1 year apart
Stringent CR: complete response plus normal FLC ratio plus no clonal cells on marrow biopsy
CR: negative immunofixation, no plasmacytomas, under 5% BM plasma cells
VGPR is 90% or more M protein reduction; PR is 50% or more; minimal response is 25-49%
keypoint_voiceover: Key numbers to memorize, MRD negativity needs a sensitivity of one in one hundred thousand cells by flow or sequencing. Complete response means negative immunofixation and under five percent marrow plasma cells. Very good partial response is a ninety percent or greater M protein drop, partial response is fifty percent or greater, and minimal response is twenty five to forty nine percent. Stringent complete response adds a normal free light chain ratio on top of complete response.
